acv.quote: About a hundred and forty K a year.

header.reason: The deal turned when Wen took one month of the customer's statements and priced the hand-matching hours and unmatched-deposit write-offs, and the CFO said 'that's my number, not yours.' Before that, the portal and checkout pitch had stalled and the rep had the deal at 20 percent.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim first-call messaging at a new CFO's slow month-end close and hand reconciliation, not the ordering portal project named in the inbound.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Build a repeatable one month of your statements workup that prices reconciliation hours and write-offs, so CFOs see their own numbers.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Arm reps to contrast a named contact with a bank incumbent's rates-only reply, and ask customers what Fiserv actually showed.
findings.quote: I didn't ask about my rates.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Open with payout reconciliation into the ERP for regional distributors, and test cutting the financial infrastructure, global growth and developer story.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a wholesale distributor reference customer and case study covering invoices and branch counter sales in one report.
findings.quote: this is a company that sells sweaters.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'know where my money is' and 'the deposits' in finance-buyer messaging instead of 'payments' and 'infrastructure'.
findings.quote: I just want to know where my money is.
